title: Rapid probe: SDK sprint template (standalone)
body:
Purpose
----
This is a lightweight, copyable sprint template to run a 1–2 hour rapid probe for an SDK onboarding or docs-first experiment. Goal: produce a shippable minimal artifact (sample app + quickstart) that lets a new engineer run an end-to-end SDK flow in ~15 minutes locally. Keep everything single-file-friendly and resilient to flaky infra.

Audience
- Engs running a proof-of-concept SDK integration
- DevEx engineers doing quick usability tests
- Solutions engineers preparing a customer demo

Outcome (must be measurable)
- 15-minute measured run: start with repo clone -> run example -> tokenized sample request -> receive streamed response (or deterministic fallback).
- Checklist: sample app runs, README < 10 steps, CI smoke test green, one telemetry event emitted, quick troubleshooting note.

Quick plan (timeboxed)
- Sprint length: 90 minutes recommended for full probe; 30–45 minutes minimal
- Roles: facilitator (owns time/decisions), implementer (writes code), doc-scribe (updates README), tester (runs test matrix) — single person can cover multiple roles for micro-sprints

Sprint agenda (90m)
- 0–10m: Kickoff and safety checks
  - Confirm environment: Node 18+ or Python 3.10+, docker availability
  - Confirm secrets: test API key available (dev key only), network allowed
  - Pick sample flow (chat, completion, embed) and target model size
- 10–40m: Implement minimal sample app
  - scaffold quickstart (index.js / main.py), single command to run
  - include env var example (.env.example)
  - implement streaming fallback: if net blocked, return canned response
- 40–55m: README + Troubleshooting micro-doc
  - 6-step README: clone, install, set key, run, expected output, verify telemetry
  - add a troubleshooting section with 3 common errors + fixes
- 55–70m: Smoke tests & CI
  - add GH Actions job matrix (node/python) with 1 test: run sample and assert substring
  - make test non-blocking in prod branch (flagged experimental)
- 70–85m: Telemetry + gating
  - emit single event: sample_start, sample_success/fail (console/log)
  - assert for privacy: no PII sent, log redaction example
- 85–90m: Wrap-up
  - capture time-to-first-response metric, decide follow-ups, file issues

Checklist (copy into PR description)
- [ ] Repo scaffolded in starter-kit branch
- [ ] index example runs locally in <= 15m from fresh clone
- [ ] README has explicit expected output (and copy-pasteable prompt)
- [ ] CI job executes sample and passes (or is gated behind experimental flag)
- [ ] Telemetry event present with schema version and sample_id
- [ ] Troubleshooting block added with 3 steps

Starter code snippets (minimal)
- Node: single-file index.js that reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from env, calls client.text.generate, streams to stdout, catches errors and prints fallback JSON. (Use simple fetch wrapper in README.)
- Python: main.py uses requests/asyncio minimal pattern, prints both streaming and final chunks.

Prompt bank (copyable)
- Small deterministic prompt: "Summarize the following in one short sentence: 

Input: The quick brown fox jumps over a lazy dog.

Output:"
- Streaming-friendly: ask for 1-2 short sentences and explicit token limit.

Telemetry invariants (must be present and small)
- event.name: sdkenv.sample_run
- event.schema: v1
- event.payload: {sample_id, runtime, duration_ms, success_bool} (log redacted - no text payload)
- Console fallback for non-instrumented runs

Failure modes and mitigations (notes to self)
- Network blocked (CI behind proxy): include non-network fallback and mock server in tests
- Large model OOM on local machine: use quantized small variant or restrict to CPU-only tiny model
- Streaming not supported in old runtimes: implement chunked-polling fallback mode
- Secrets leaked in CI logs: add mask and redact plugin in GH Actions

PR description template (short)
- Context: what user flow this unlocks
- What I changed: single-file example, README, CI job, telemetry
- How I tested: local run steps + CI run link
- Risks: none (dev-key only), follow-ups: add multi-lang examples, hardened telemetry schema

Handoff & follow-ups (light)
- Owner to pick up: doc-scribe (add to docs nav under "Quickstarts -> 15m starter")
- Follow-up tickets: add language bindings, add canary in hosted docs site, create recorded 5-min demo

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep examples tiny: newcomers bail out after step 3 if there are too many deps
- Prefer copy-paste prompts rather than long explanation blocks
- Keep telemetry optional but present locally so we can measure adoption without sampling biases

Links & references
- Quickstart reference: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEXP/Quickstart+Patterns
- Starter kit repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter-kit (PR template above)

Open questions (to resolve during sprint)
- Should the CI test run against hosted test infra or local mock by default? (mock is safer)
- Standardize stream-to-stdout behavior across languages? create small shim in sdk-utils?

TODO (short)
- [ ] Add example for embedding + similarity search (micro)
- [ ] Add minimal Dockerfile for offline demo
- [ ] Convert README example into a single playground blob for docs site

——
If you run this and get stuck, ping #devexp-quickstarts on Slack with the sprint branch name and we’ll triage live.
